track: Warm prospects — broader re-engagement and response
track_strategy: Reopen the broader warm list without borrowing the selected-preview invitation. The sequence moves from a cold-reader reintroduction to a short visual, approved operating proof, and one direct invitation. Once someone responds, campaign language stops and Mark continues from the context already provided. Every email has one primary action and keeps ordinary engagement separate from a sales handoff.
open_questions: Jane should confirm the neutral trigger for opening the broader warm cycle.
What shorter follow-up should selected-preview recipients receive instead of WARM-REENGAGE-01, and should Mark send it personally?
Confirm [LUCI UPGRADE GUIDE URL], [FEATURE HIGHLIGHT REEL URL], [FULL RECORDING URL], [PROOF URL], [BOOKING URL], and [MARK EMAIL].
Approve each project-true consolidation count inserted for [APPROVED PROOF POINT] before WARM-REENGAGE-03 enters review.
Who should be the named sender for WARM-REENGAGE-01 through 04?
Should WARM-RESPONSE-01 come from Marketing or from the LUCI contact who receives the response?

emails.title: What changed
emails.timing: When Marketing opens the broader warm cycle
emails.audience: Broader warm contacts who did not receive the selected preview and remain outside active sales conversations
emails.primary_message: A cold reader sees the problem first: one wrong screen should not require several interfaces and an off-site expert.

strategy.what_why: A true reintroduction for the broader warm list, built around a familiar failure rather than selective access.
strategy.for_whom: Past contacts who may barely remember LUCI and did not receive the private-preview invitation.
strategy.reach: Open on one wrong screen after hours, define LUCI and the beta change, then make the guide the one primary action.
strategy.impact: Use a specific failure scene and show how direct screen checks, activity history, and continued LUCI support change the response.

directions.name: The 9:12 p.m. screen
directions.summary: Reintroduce LUCI through one wrong-screen incident after hours.
directions.draft:
Dear #Name#,

At 9:12 p.m., a screen shows the wrong source. The right control sits in another interface, and the person who usually fixes it is off site. That is too much plot for one screen.

LUCI orchestrates a property’s A/V through one interface; New LUCI is in beta and lets staff confirm live screen content, make approved changes, and check the activity record while our team keeps monitoring, diagnosing, and supporting.

See the details in the LUCI Upgrade Guide: [LUCI UPGRADE GUIDE URL]

directions.name: One wrong wall
directions.summary: Use a visible failure to show why another look matters.
directions.draft:

LUCI consolidates property A/V into one interface. New LUCI is in beta and adds direct screen checks, approved controls, and activity history for on-site staff, with our team still monitoring and supporting the platform.

The wall is complicated enough. The response should not be.

Read the LUCI Upgrade Guide: [LUCI UPGRADE GUIDE URL]

directions.name: Skip the interface hunt
directions.summary: Open on the cost of searching across systems and people.

No interface scavenger hunt required.

Review the LUCI Upgrade Guide: [LUCI UPGRADE GUIDE URL]

emails.why_won: It gives the broader re-engagement a distinct problem-first opening, assumes no memory, and explains the beta through a recognizable incident rather than replaying preview scenes.
